reciprocityRules.value: Utah has exactly one formal, no-examination bilateral reciprocal agreement for journeyman electricians: with Oregon (Utah DOPL / Oregon Building Codes Division Agreement BCD# 73-0-452). Under this agreement, Utah issues a Journeyman Electrician license WITHOUT EXAMINATION to a holder of an Oregon journeyman electrician license/certificate (and Oregon reciprocates for Utah journeyman holders), provided: the original license was obtained BY EXAMINATION with a minimum score of 75%; it is current, active, and in good standing; and it was earned via at least 4 years (8,000 hours) of electrical trade experience under direct supervision of a licensed journeyman, plus completion of a 4-year electrical apprenticeship vocational education program (minimum 576 classroom hours) — or experience/education independently determined equivalent by the licensing state. All reciprocity applicants must still pay the required fees to the reviewing state. No other state-specific no-exam reciprocal agreement was found for Utah journeyman licensure; for every other state, applicants use Utah's broader ENDORSEMENT pathway instead (see endorsementRules), which does not guarantee an examination waiver.

reciprocityRules.notes: A commonly repeated secondary-source claim (multiple contractor-license aggregator blogs — servicetitan.com, contractorlicenserequirements.com, ultimateelectriciansguide.com, sparkshift.app, and others) states Utah has bilateral reciprocity with Arizona, Nevada, Idaho, Colorado, and Wyoming. This was actively investigated: the official DOPL 'equivalent states' endorsement-map PDFs referenced by the Journeyman and Master out-of-state-by-endorsement pages (endorsement-to-utah-journeyman-electrician.pdf, endorsement-to-utah-master-electrician.pdf) returned HTTP 403 on every automated fetch attempt (multiple tries, including a retry after the user manually accessed the surrounding HTML pages), and no official source confirming or denying this specific 5-state list was found anywhere. Even the search-engine synthesis of secondary sources flagged internal contradictions on this exact claim. It is NOT included as fact here — absence of confirmation is treated as absence, not silently assumed true. This gap should be revisited if the endorsement-map PDFs become reachable.

endorsementRules.value: For any state OTHER than Oregon, an out-of-state journeyman electrician license holder must apply through Utah's general licensure-BY-ENDORSEMENT pathway (Utah Code 58-1-302; Utah Admin. Code R156-1-302, incorporated for electricians via R156-55b-305), not the narrower no-exam reciprocity pathway. Under this pathway, the license does not need to still be currently active, and the Division evaluates whether the applicant's prior licensed/lawful practice is still substantively relevant. However, R156-1-302 states the Division MAY require the applicant to pass one or more exams (business/law, jurisprudence, or professional) 'except if expressly provided otherwise in statute or rule' — meaning, unlike Oregon reciprocity, an examination is NOT guaranteed to be waived for endorsement applicants from other states.

endorsementRules.notes: Utah is the first of PermitBridge's electrician states where 'reciprocity' and 'endorsement' are genuinely distinct, separately governed pathways rather than interchangeable terminology — every prior state (Colorado, Virginia, Texas, Arkansas, Minnesota) left this field Unknown because no such distinction existed in their materials. Confidence set to 'likely' rather than 'verified' because the citation is a third-party (Cornell LII) mirror of the rule text, not Utah's own .gov page, which was unreachable throughout this research.

requiredExams.value: Via the Oregon RECIPROCITY pathway: no additional Utah examination — the agreement issues the license 'without examination' provided the original Oregon exam score was at least 75%. Via the general ENDORSEMENT pathway (all other states): Utah Admin. Code R156-1-302 gives the Division discretion to require the applicant pass one or more exams, so a waiver is not guaranteed for journeyman endorsement applicants. Whether journeyman endorsement specifically always requires a Utah-specific exam (as master endorsement explicitly does — see utah-master.json) was not independently confirmed; not assumed to be identical to master's confirmed requirement without direct source text from the Journeyman Out-of-State by Endorsement page, which returned HTTP 403 on every automated fetch.
